title: Twelve Digging Seasons and One Lost Tooth
subtitle: 古生物与进化 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 古生物与进化（自然生态·古生物与进化）
meta: 主题语境：古生物与进化（自然生态·古生物与进化）　|　核心词汇：dinosaur　|　正文 340 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 dinosaur 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1948 the excavator ① found a dinosaur that no museum in the province would have housed, and he said the finding was the whole of the season. The ② dinosaur, meaning the animal and not the bone, ran twelve digging seasons and stayed unnamed in the crate; a dinosaur, he said, is the only thing in a quarry that is judged by how long it is left unmeasured.

Every ③ dinosaur in that quarry had the same lost tooth beside it, and the ④ dinosaur at the end, meaning the one they kept for the school cases and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever measured twice. A dinosaur, his assistant said, is nine parts plaster and one part somebody willing to dig; the excavator said the digging is the part that fills twelve seasons.

The curator meant the other thing entirely: she said ⑤ the dinosaur was the whole of the gallery, meaning the skeleton and not the animal. The ⑥ dinosaur, meaning the skeleton and not any of that, is the only thing in a gallery that everybody photographs and nobody questions; dinosaur, she said, is either something you find or the only word that means both an animal and a skeleton. She said the skeleton is the part they remember.

By 1957 the ⑦ dinosaur had become a line in a register, and the register had become an argument about the lost tooth. The ⑧ dinosaur of the whole thing, the excavator wrote in June, was one quarry and twelve seasons of digging; dinosaur, he said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to dig. She said the digging was never mentioned.

The ⑨ dinosaur I remember is the one at the end, which was mounted in 1971 and is still described as the largest in the province. A ⑩ dinosaur, the assistant said in 1973, is the only thing that improves by being measured; every dinosaur, she said, is a skeleton that has agreed to look like an animal. She said the skeleton was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 恐龙（指采石场里挖出的那一只）
B. n. 恐龙（指那头动物本身，与那具骨架相对）
C. 固定搭配：find a dinosaur 发现一只恐龙（化石）
D. n. 恐龙（指留给学校展柜用的那一只）
E. n. 恐龙；恐龙化石（抽象总称，指一处采石场的全部发掘）
F. n. 恐龙（指登记簿上写到、被列名的那一只）
G. n. 恐龙骨架；化石标本（指展廊里立起的那具）
H. n. 骨架（抽象总称，指人人拍照却无人追问的那具）

items.q: found a dinosaur that no museum in the province would have housed
The dinosaur, meaning the animal and not the bone
the dinosaur was the whole of the gallery
the dinosaur had become a line in a register
The dinosaur of the whole thing
A dinosaur, the assistant said in 1973

answers.why: find a dinosaur 意为“发现一只恐龙（化石）”，1948 年发掘者发现了一只全省没有一家博物馆肯收藏的恐龙。
dinosaur 意为“恐龙”，指那头动物本身而不是那块骨头，它历经十二个挖掘季而在木箱里没有名字。
dinosaur 意为“恐龙”，指那处采石场里每一只恐龙，每一只旁边都有同一颗遗失的牙。
dinosaur 意为“恐龙”，指留给学校展柜用的那一只，是唯一有人量过两次的。
dinosaur 意为“恐龙骨架、化石标本”，指展廊里立起的那具，馆长说这具标本就是那条展廊的全部。
dinosaur 意为“骨架”，指人人拍照却无人追问的那具而不是那头动物本身，是展廊里人人都拍照、却无人追问的东西。
dinosaur 意为“恐龙”，指登记簿上写到、被列名的那一只，到 1957 年这只恐龙成了登记簿里的一行。
dinosaur 意为“恐龙、恐龙化石”，发掘者六月写道，整件事的发掘是一处采石场和十二个季节的挖掘。
dinosaur 意为“恐龙”，我记得的是末尾那一只，1971 年被架起，至今仍被说成全省最大的一只。
dinosaur 为抽象总称，助手 1973 年说，一只恐龙是唯一会因为被测量而变得更好的东西。
